Work through these checks in order, and record what you actually observe for each:
1. At the narrow viewport, focus each minus, plus, reset, submit, and modal-close button with the keyboard. Then Tab through the controls and observe the focused control each time. — expect: Each focused control must have a clearly visible focus indicator and remain identifiable by its row or purpose.
2. Resize the viewport to about 320px wide and inspect the complete audit table and action controls. Then Read every SKU, item, System, Counted, Variance, Reset, and Submit control at that width. — expect: All table values and controls must be readable and reachable without clipping or overlap.
3. Set the SECOND row to 59 and the FOURTH row to 9, then record those displayed values. Then Click Reset counts, submit, and close the confirmation dialog. — expect: Reset must leave all rows at system counts; submission and dismissal must not restore stale edited values.
4. Open the submission dialog. Then Close it with the button, reopen it, press Escape, reopen it, then click the backdrop outside the dialog. — expect: Each dismissal method must close the dialog; each reopening must show it again.
5. Leave all counts at their initial values. Then Click Submit audit once. — expect: A visible dialog must appear with the heading “Audit s

verifications.claim: Each item’s inline stepper changes that same item’s Counted value by one and updates its Variance correspondingly.
verifications.evidence: Steps 5 and 7 show the controls listed/rendered for Washer 11mm changing Hex bolt M4 instead (140→139/−1 and 140→141/+1) while Washer remained 60/—; step 21 likewise records the attempted Cable 2m decrement leaving Cable at 18/— and changing Washer to 59/−1.

verifications.claim: Reset counts restores all four Counted values to their System values and clears every Variance to an em dash.
verifications.evidence: After Reset counts, step 10 records Hex bolt 140, Washer 60, Cable 18, and Panel 7, with every variance shown as an em dash; step 20 independently records the same all-row reset state.

verifications.claim: Submitting an audit opens a visible Audit submitted confirmation dialog over the audit table while preserving the changed row behind it.
verifications.evidence: Step 22 records that Submit audit produced a visible modal and dark backdrop, with the underlying table still visible and the changed Washer row at 59/−1; step 24 records the dialog message as visible on a subsequent submission.

verifications.claim: The confirmation dialog can be dismissed with Close, by clicking the backdrop, and with Escape, returning the user to the audit table.
verifications.evidence: Steps 22–23 show Close removing the dialog and backdrop; steps 24–25 show backdrop click removing them; and steps 26–27 show Escape returning to the table with no dialog or backdrop.

verifications.claim: Keyboard Tab focus remains trapped on dialog controls and never leaves the confirmation dialog while it is open.
verifications.evidence: After Tab moved focus to the dialog Close button in step 29, the next Tab observation in step 30 found the modal still open but no visible focus indicator on Close or any dialog control, so focus did not remain on the dialog’s sole control.

verifications.claim: At a narrow mobile viewport, every audit table label, value, stepper, and bottom action remains readable and reachable without clipping or overlap.
verifications.evidence: The run did not resize to a mobile viewport; step 36 explicitly states that mobile viewport resizing was not supported by the provided action set.

findingTexts: Modal focus is not trapped. With the Audit submitted dialog open, pressing Tab three times moved focus to the underlying Hex bolt M4 minus button while the modal remained visible.
Intended Washer/Cable steppers update their own rows, but Washer clicks alter Hex and Cable minus alters Washer.

plan.expect: Counted must change by one and variance must change correspondingly, then both must return to their noted values.

plan.setup: Change Washer 11mm with minus and Panel A3 with plus; record both altered counts.
plan.action: Click Reset counts and reread every row.
plan.expect: All counted values must equal their System values and every Variance must show an em dash.

plan.setup: Change the non-first Cable 2m count once and note its displayed variance.
plan.action: Click Submit audit and read the confirmation dialog.
plan.expect: A visible dialog must appear with the stated submission message while the changed row remains visible behind it.

plan.setup: Open the confirmation dialog by submitting the audit.
plan.action: Click Close, submit again, click the dark backdrop, submit again, then press Escape.
plan.expect: Each dismissal method must close the dialog and return to the audit table.

plan.setup: Open the confirmation dialog and press Tab repeatedly without clicking the page.
plan.action: Observe the focused elements while cycling through the dialog.
plan.expect: Focus must remain on dialog controls and must never move to the underlying audit controls.

plan.setup: Set the viewport to a narrow mobile width and reload the audit page.
plan.action: Read all table headers, item names, counts, variances, and both bottom buttons.
plan.expect: Every label, value, stepper, and action must be readable and reachable without being clipped or covered.

plan.action: Reload the audit page after changing a count but before submitting.
plan.expect: The page must clearly follow its persistence rule; if counts are transient, they must reset to System values.
